# Volume 1 — CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

“WHAT a magnificent day!” Nell remarked, taking a deep breath. “Is it not wonderful merely to exist on such a day? My heart goes out to the unborn who are absent from it. Naturally, they might experience fine days, but this specific one is forever out of their reach. Furthermore, having a route to school that is so delightful makes it even more magnificent, does it not?”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0000 }

“Traveling this way is much pleasant than taking the road, which is very dusty and warm,” Isolde remarked pragmatically, glancing inside her lunch basket while calculating in her head how many bites every girl would get if the trio of succulent, delicious raspberry tarts sitting inside were shared among ten girls.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0001 }

The young female students at Brierley school invariably combined their mid-day meals, meaning that if a girl consumed three raspberry tarts completely by herself, or merely split them with her closest friend, she would be perpetually labeled as “awful mean” by the others. However, splitting those tarts between ten girls resulted in a portion that merely teased your appetite.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0002 }

The route that Nell and Isolde took to school was lovely. Nell felt that it was impossible even to imagine a better walk to and from school than the one she shared with Isolde. Taking the main road would have lacked romance completely; conversely, traveling via Linger Lane, Reedmere, Primrose Dell, and the Aspen Path was the very definition of romance.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0003 }

Below the orchard at Grey Shutters, Linger Lane commenced its course, extending deep into the forest until it reached the edge of the Abernethy farm. The cattle were driven along this path to the rear field, and during the winter season, timber was transported back by it. Prior to completing a month at Grey Shutters, Nell had bestowed the name Linger Lane upon it.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0004 }

“It isn't as if lovers actually stroll along it,” she clarified to Thirza, “yet Isolde and I happen to be enjoying an absolutely marvelous novel that features a Linger Lane. Because of that, we wish to possess one as well. Also, the name possesses a great deal of charm, wouldn't you agree? It is so full of romance! You see, we are unable to picture the lovers inside it. My fondness for that lane stems from the fact that you may speak your thoughts openly there and not have people brand you as insane.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0005 }

Setting off by herself when morning came, Nell traveled along Linger Lane until she reached the brook. Isolde joined her at this spot, and together the two young girls continued traveling up the lane beneath a green canopy of maples—“maples are such friendly trees,” Nell remarked; “they constantly rustle and whisper in your ear”—before arriving at a wooden bridge. Leaving the lane behind, they proceeded across Mr. Pembroke’s back field and traveled past Reedmere. Lying past Reedmere was Primrose Dell—a small, verdant hollow shaded by Mr. Andrew Bell’s large forest. “Naturally, no violets grow there at present,” Nell mentioned to Thirza, “yet Isolde claims millions bloom during springtime. Oh, Thirza, isn't it easy to picture them right before your eyes? It truly makes me gasp. I gave it the name Primrose Dell. Isolde remarks that no one surpasses me when it comes to devising imaginative names for locations. Having a talent for something is wonderful, wouldn't you say? However, Isolde chose the name for the Aspen Path. Because she wished to, I permitted her; nevertheless, I know I could have devised a phrase more artistic than just Aspen Path. Anyone is capable of inventing a title of that sort. Even so, the Aspen Path ranks among the most lovely spots anywhere, Thirza.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0006 }

Indeed it was. When others chanced upon it, their opinion matched Nell’s. That small, pinched, snaking track sloped downward across a lengthy hill, passing directly through Mr. Bell’s woods, a place where the sunlight filtered through numerous green canopies until it matched the perfection found at the center of a diamond. Tall, graceful birches boasting pale trunks lined every inch of its borders; a dense growth of ferns, starflowers, wild lilies-of-the-valley, and bright red clumps of pigeonberries stretched beside it; moreover, a pleasing aromatic scent continually filled the atmosphere alongside avian melodies and the gentle rustle and chuckle of breeze moving through the upper branches. Occasionally, a calm observer could spot a rabbit darting over the dirt—an occurrence that took place very rarely when Nell and Isolde were present. Reaching the valley bottom, the trail emerged onto the primary thoroughfare, leaving only the pine-covered incline to climb before reaching the school.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0007 }

A whitewashed structure featuring low eaves and broad windows housed the Brierley school, containing comfortable, sturdy, old-fashioned desks on the inside that opened and closed, their lids entirely covered in carvings of initials and hieroglyphics from three generations of pupils. Positioned back from the road, the schoolhouse had a dark fir wood to its rear alongside a stream where every child placed their milk bottles during the morning so they would remain cold and fresh through lunchtime.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0008 }

With numerous hidden anxieties, Thirza had watched Nell depart for school on the first of September. Nell was a very strange girl. In what way would she interact with the rest of the children? And by what possible means could she succeed in keeping quiet throughout the time class was in session?
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0009 }

Matters proceeded more favorably than Thirza had anticipated, nevertheless. Nell returned to the house that night in great delight.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0010 }

“I believe this school will suit me,” she declared. “However, I do not hold a high opinion of the teacher. He continuously twirls his mustache and casts romantic glances toward Sukey Pullen. Sukey is an adult, as you are aware. Her age is sixteen, and she is preparing for the Regent’s Academy entrance exam in Port Marlow for the coming year. Tillie Gammon claims that the teacher is hopelessly in love with her. Her skin is lovely, her brown hair is curly, and her hairstyle is arranged so stylishly. Her spot is at the back on the long bench, and he spends the majority of his time seated there as well—claiming it is to clarify her coursework. Nevertheless, Opal Pettigrew claims she caught him scribbling a message on her slate, which made Sukey flush bright red and laugh nervously upon reading it; and Opal Pettigrew claims she doubts that it pertained to the coursework at all.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0011 }

“Nell Harcourt, stop speaking of your teacher like that this instant,” Thirza reprimanded. “Attending school to find fault with the master is not why you are there. Surely he has knowledge to impart, and your duty is to absorb it. Furthermore, get it into your head immediately that bringing home gossip regarding him is forbidden. Such behavior will receive no support from me. Were you well-behaved, I trust?”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0012 }

“Indeed I was,” said Nell comfortably. “It was not as difficult as you might think, either. I share a seat with Isolde. Positioned right beside the window, our seat lets us look down at the Lake of Glassy Waters. The school contains many nice girls, and we had scrumptious fun playing during dinnertime. Having many little girls to play with is so nice. However, I naturally like Isolde best and always will. I adore Isolde. I am dreadfully far behind everyone else. Everyone else is in the fifth book while I am merely in the fourth. I feel as though it is somewhat of a disgrace. Nevertheless, not a single one of them possesses an imagination like mine, a fact I quickly discovered. Today, we had reading, geography, Canadian history, and dictation. Mr. Pidgeon stated that my spelling was disgraceful, holding up my slate, all covered in marks, so that everyone could see. Thirza, I felt so mortified; I think he could have shown more politeness to a stranger. An apple was given to me by Opal Pettigrew, and Sophia Mott lent me a lovely pink card bearing the words ‘May I see you home?’. I must return it to her tomorrow. Furthermore, Tillie Gammon permitted me to wear her bead ring for the entire afternoon. May I take a few of those pearl beads from the old pincushion in the garret so I can craft a ring for myself? And oh, Thirza, Odette Pullen disclosed to me that Posy MacKinnon told her she overheard Sukey Pullen tell Sara Pettigrew that my nose was very pretty. Thirza, that marks the very first compliment I have ever received in my life, and the strange feeling it imparted to me is beyond your imagination. Thirza, do I truly possess a pretty nose? I know that you will speak the truth to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0013 }

“Your nose is fine as it is,” Thirza replied abruptly. In truth, she considered Nell’s nose to be exceptionally attractive; however, she was determined not to let her know that.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0014 }

Three weeks had passed since that time, with everything proceeding without a hitch up to this point. Now, on a cool September morning, Isolde and Nell were walking briskly and cheerfully along the Aspen Path, being a pair of the most joyful young girls in Brierley.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0015 }

“I suppose Hugh Carrow is going to be at school today,” Isolde remarked. “All summer long he’s been over in New Brunswick visiting his cousins, and Saturday night was when he finally returned home. Nell, he’s terribly handsome. And the way he teases the girls is just awful. He simply makes our lives a misery.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0016 }

Isolde’s tone of voice suggested that she was somewhat fond of having her life plagued out of her instead of the alternative.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0017 }

“Hugh Carrow?” Nell asked. “Isn’t he the one whose name is inscribed on the wall of the porch alongside Julia Bell’s, with a large ‘Take Notice’ above them both?”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0018 }

“Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0019 }

“Oh, do not mention freckles to me,” begged Nell. “When I have such a quantity, it lacks delicacy. However, I truly believe that scribbling notices regarding the boys and girls on the wall is the most ridiculous thing possible. I would simply love to watch anyone have the courage to write my name alongside a boy’s. Not, naturally,” she was quick to insert, “that anyone ever would.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0020 }

Nell let out a sigh. Having her name recorded was something she preferred to avoid. Even so, realizing that she faced no risk at all of it happening felt somewhat humiliating.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0021 }

“Nonsense,” stated Isolde, the individual whose dark eyes and shiny hair had so thoroughly disrupted the emotions of Brierley schoolboys that her name was displayed in six different take-notices on the porch walls. “A joke is all it is intended to be. And you shouldn't feel so certain that a time will never come when your name is scribbled somewhere. Wilfred Mott is completely infatuated with you. It was to his mother—take note, his mother—that he declared you were the cleverest female student in the whole school. Having that said about you surpasses being attractive.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0022 }

“It is not, though,” Nell remarked, being entirely feminine. “Being pretty is what I would choose over being clever. Also, Wilfred Mott is someone I detest, as I cannot tolerate a boy whose eyes goggle. Isolde Pembroke, I would be permanently ruined if my name were written alongside his by anyone. Even so, remaining at the top of one's class is a pleasant thing.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0023 }

“Following this, Hugh will join your class,” Isolde remarked, “and I can assure you that he is accustomed to leading his class. Despite being almost fourteen, he is merely in the fourth book. Four years back, his father fell ill and was forced to travel to Alberta for his well-being, taking Hugh along. Their stay lasted three years, during which Hughie scarcely attended school at all prior to their return. Nell, maintaining your position at the top will not be nearly as simple now.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0024 }

“I’m happy,” Nell stated rapidly. “Being at the top of a class of young children who are only nine or ten years old wouldn't truly make me feel proud. Yesterday, I moved up to the head by spelling ‘ebullition.’ Flossie Tulk was at the top, and I'm telling you, she sneaked a look at her book. Mr. Pidgeon missed it—his eyes were on Sukey Pullen—however, I caught her. I simply threw her an icy, contemptuous glance, causing her to turn as red as a beetroot, and she ended up spelling it incorrectly anyway.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0025 }

“Every one of those Tulk girls acts dishonestly,” Isolde remarked with irritation while they scaled the main road's fence. “Yesterday, Tibby Tulk literally set her milk bottle where mine belonged in the brook. Can you imagine? Now I refuse to talk to her.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0026 }

As Mr. Pidgeon listened to Sukey Pullen recite her Latin from the rear of the classroom, Isolde leaned over to Nell and murmured, “Directly across the aisle from you sits Hugh Carrow, Nell. Take a glance at him and tell me whether you find him attractive.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0027 }

Nell observed in response. She possessed an excellent opportunity for this, as the mentioned Hugh Carrow was fully occupied with quietly attaching the lengthy blonde plait belonging to Opal Pettigrew, who was seated before him, to her chair's back. He was a high-statured youth, possessing wavy chestnut hair, mischievous light-brown eyes, and a mouth contorted into a mocking grin. Before long, Opal Pettigrew rose abruptly to bring an arithmetic problem to the teacher; she collapsed back onto her chair with a faint scream, under the impression that her hair had been yanked out at the roots. All the students gazed in her direction and Mr. Pidgeon stared with such severity that Opal started weeping. Hugh had swiftly hidden the pin and was reading his history lesson with an utterly serious expression; however, once the disturbance quieted down, he caught Nell's eye and winked with boundless humor.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0028 }

“In my opinion, your Hugh Carrow has good looks,” Nell admitted to Isolde, “yet I find his behavior quite daring. Winking at an unfamiliar girl violates proper etiquette.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0029 }

However, real events did not truly start unfolding until afternoon arrived.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0030 }

Mr. Pidgeon had returned to the corner where he was clarifying an algebraic problem for Sukey Pullen, while the remaining students were behaving largely as they liked by consuming green apples, speaking softly, sketching images on their slates, and steering crickets attached to strings along the aisle. Hugh Carrow was attempting to gain Nell Harcourt’s attention without any success, since Nell was then completely unaware not merely of the presence of Hugh Carrow, but of all the other pupils within Brierley school as well. Supporting her chin with her hands while resting her eyes on the small blue view of the Lake of Glassy Waters visible through the west window, she had drifted into a magnificent realm of fantasy, perceiving and witnessing only her own extraordinary imaginations.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0031 }

It was not Hugh Carrow’s habit to exert himself to attract a girl's gaze only to be unsuccessful. That red-haired Harcourt girl, who possessed the small pointed chin along with the large eyes that differed from those of every other girl at Brierley school, ought to look at him.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0032 }

Hugh extended his arm over the space between their seats, took hold of the tip of Nell’s lengthy crimson plait, stretched it as far as his arm could reach, and uttered in an intense whisper:
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0033 }

“Carrots! Carrots!”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0034 }

At that point, Nell glared at him intensely!
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0035 }

She went beyond merely gazing. Rising abruptly to her feet, she saw her brilliant imaginations shattered beyond repair. From eyes where a furious gleaming was rapidly drowned by tears of matching rage, she shot a single wrathful look toward Hugh.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0036 }

“You vile, spiteful youth!” she cried out with deep emotion. “How could you!”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0037 }

And next—thwack! bringing her slate down upon Hugh’s head, Nell broke it—the slate, not the head—straight in two.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0038 }

A commotion was always welcomed at Brierley school. The present one proved particularly delicious. "Oh," everyone uttered with scandalized pleasure. A gasp came from Isolde. Prone to hysteria, Opal Pettigrew started weeping. His mouth agape at the scene, Tommy Mott allowed his collection of crickets to get away from him completely.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0039 }

Mr. Pidgeon marched down the aisle, placing his hand firmly upon the shoulder of Nell.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0040 }

“Nell Harcourt, what is the meaning of this?” he asked in an angry tone. Nell made no reply. Expecting her to admit in front of the entire school that someone had called her “carrots” was asking too much of flesh and blood. Hugh was the one who bravely spoke out.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0041 }

“Mr. Pidgeon, the blame belongs to me because I provoked her.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0042 }

Hugh was completely ignored by Mr. Pidgeon.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0043 }

“It grieves me to observe a student under my instruction showing this kind of rage and this sort of revengeful attitude,” he remarked with grave gravity, as though just having him as a teacher should eradicate every bad impulse from the minds of young flawed human beings. “Nell, proceed to the dais before the blackboard and remain standing there throughout the remainder of the day.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0044 }

A beating would have been vastly favored by Nell over this penalty, which made her tender soul shudder as if struck by a whip. She complied, her countenance pale and rigid. Above her head, Mr. Pidgeon utilized a piece of chalk to write upon the blackboard.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0045 }

“Ann Harcourt possesses an extremely poor temper. Ann Harcourt is required to learn temper control,” and subsequently uttered the sentence aloud so it would be intelligible even to the primer class, who were unable to read handwriting.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0046 }

Nell remained standing there with that inscription over her head for the remainder of the afternoon. She neither wept nor bowed her head. The rage in her heart remained too intense for such reactions, supporting her through the full anguish of her shame. With a furious stare and cheeks flushed with passion, she faced Isolde’s compassionate look, Wilfred Mott’s angry nods, and Flossie Tulk’s spiteful grins with equal defiance. Regarding Hugh Carrow, she refused to so much as glance in his direction. Never again would she cast her eyes upon him! Never again would she utter a word to him!!
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0047 }

As soon as classes ended, Nell walked out, holding her red-haired head erect. At the doorway to the porch, Hugh Carrow attempted to block her path.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0048 }

“Nell, I’m terribly apologetic about mocking your hair,” he murmured remorsefully. “Truly I am. Please don’t stay angry forever.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0049 }

Nell brushed past haughtily, failing to glance at him or show any indication that she had heard. “Oh how could you, Nell?” whispered Isolde while they walked along the road, her tone blending slight rebuke with a degree of wonder. Isolde believed that it would have been impossible for her to turn down Hugh’s entreaty.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0050 }

“Hugh Carrow is someone I will never forgive,” Nell declared with conviction. “Furthermore, my name was written minus the final e by Mr. Pidgeon as well. Isolde, the iron has pierced my very soul.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0051 }

While Isolde was completely ignorant of Nell’s meaning, she nevertheless grasped that it signified a dreadful thing.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0052 }

“You must not be upset by Hugh teasing you about your hair,” she stated to comfort me. “Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0053 }

“It is quite a distinct matter to be named a crow compared to being named carrots,” Nell stated solemnly. “My feelings have been injured most agonizingly by Hugh Carrow, Isolde.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0054 }

The situation perhaps could have settled down without further agony had no additional events occurred. However, once incidents commence, they tend to persist.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0055 }

Students from Brierley frequently passed the midday break collecting gum within the spruce wood belonging to Mr. Bell, located beyond the hill and past his large pasture. This vantage point allowed them to watch the residence of Eben Duckett, the location of the master's lodgings. As soon as Mr. Pidgeon was observed stepping out of it, a race toward the schoolhouse commenced; however, because that journey measured roughly thrice the length of Mr. Duckett’s lane, reaching the destination out of breath and panting approximately three minutes after the time limit was a common occurrence.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0056 }

During the next day, Mr. Pidgeon had a sudden impulse to enforce discipline, declaring prior to his departure for dinner at home that he anticipated every student would be occupying their assigned seat upon his comeback. A penalty would be given to anybody arriving after the set time.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0057 }

As was their habit, every boy and a portion of the girls headed to Mr. Bell’s spruce grove, thoroughly purposing to remain just until they could “pick a chew.” Nevertheless, spruce groves hold temptation and yellow gum nuts possess charm; they gathered, lingered, and wandered; and, as was customary, what first awakened them to how quickly time had passed was Jimmy Glover yelling “Master’s coming” while perched atop an ancient, patriarchal spruce.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0058 }

Those girls who were already on the ground set off first, succeeding in getting to the schoolhouse just in time with not a single second to spare. The boys, needing to scramble down from the trees in a hurry, were behind them; while Nell, who had been strolling joyfully at the distant end of the grove instead of gathering gum, buried up to her waist in the bracken, quietly singing to herself, wearing a crown of rice lilies in her hair like a wild spirit of the shaded woods, was the very last. Nevertheless, Nell was able to run as fast as a deer; run she indeed did, producing the mischievous outcome of catching up with the boys at the entrance and being carried into the schoolhouse right in the middle of them precisely when Mr. Pidgeon was hanging up his hat.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0059 }

The fleeting impulse for reform that had seized Mr. Pidgeon had passed; he preferred not to go through the trouble of disciplining twelve students; nevertheless, action was required to preserve his reputation, which led him to search for a victim, discovering one in Nell, who had slumped into her chair, breathless, while an overlooked garland of lilies dangled sideways above a single ear, bestowing upon her a remarkably untidy and jaunty air.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0060 }

“Nell Harcourt, because you appear to take such pleasure in the presence of the boys, we will satisfy your desire for it later today,” he remarked with sarcasm. “Remove those blossoms from your hair and take a seat next to Hugh Carrow.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0061 }

A giggle came from the rest of the boys. Whitenings of compassion washed over Isolde as she pulled the wreath off Nell’s hair and gave her hand a squeeze. Turned seemingly to stone, Nell fixed her gaze upon the master.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0062 }

“Nell, did you hear my words?” Mr. Pidgeon asked in a stern manner.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0063 }

“Indeed, sir,” Nell uttered unhurriedly, “however, I failed to assume that your intentions were genuine.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0064 }

“I assure you I did”—he maintained the mocking tone that every child, particularly Nell, detested. It stung an open wound. “Obey me at once.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0065 }

Nell appeared momentarily on the verge of refusal. However, acknowledging the inevitability of the situation, she stood up proudly, walked over the aisle, took a seat next to Hugh Carrow, and hid her face within her arms upon the desk. Opal Pettigrew, catching a brief sight of her face while it descended, informed the other children on their way back from school that she had “acksually never seen anything like it—it was so white, with awful little red spots in it.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0066 }

For Nell, this felt like the utter conclusion of everything. Being selected for disciplinary action out of twelve peers who shared identical guilt was terrible in itself; being forced to occupy a seat beside a boy was even worse, yet the fact that the male student was Hugh Carrow added an utterly intolerable level of offense to her existing misfortune. Nell was convinced that enduring this was beyond her capacity, and making an effort would serve no purpose. Shame, wrath, and degradation churned throughout her entire spirit.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0067 }

Initially, the remaining students stared, murmured, laughed softly, and poked one another. However, because Nell refrained from raising her eyes and Hugh solved math problems as though his entire spirit was concentrated solely on them, the pupils shortly went back to their individual work, leaving Nell ignored. When the history lesson was summoned by Mr. Pidgeon, Nell ought to have attended, yet she remained seated, while Mr. Pidgeon, who was composing a poem titled “To Honora” prior to calling the group, remained preoccupied with a stubborn rhyme and failed to notice her absence. At one point, while no one was watching, Hugh extracted a small pink confection heart bearing a gilded message, “You are sweet,” from his desk and slid it beneath the bend of Nell’s arm. At this, Nell stood up, held the pink candy delicately with her fingertips, let it fall to the ground, crushed it into dust under her shoe, and sat back down as before without condescending to look at Hugh.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0068 }

Upon the conclusion of class, Nell proceeded to her workspace, where she made a point of withdrawing all her belongings, including her books and notepad, pen and inkwell, testament and math text, stacking them orderly atop her fractured slate.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0069 }

“Nell, why are you bringing all those items back with you?” inquired Isolde, the moment they reached the road, having lacked the courage to pose the query earlier.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0070 }

“I am not coming back to school any more,” Nell declared. Isolde caught her breath and gazed at Nell, trying to discern if she was serious.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0071 }

“Will Thirza permit you to remain at home?” was her question.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0072 }

“She will be forced to,” declared Nell. “I am never returning to school to be taught by that man.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0073 }

“Oh, Nell!” Isolde appeared on the verge of tears. “I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0074 }

“I’d perform nearly any act on earth on your behalf, Isolde,” Nell uttered mournfully. “I’d suffer being ripped apart piece by piece if that might benefit you. However, this is beyond what I can do, so I beg you not to request it. You deeply torment my innermost spirit.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0075 }

“Only consider the amount of enjoyment you are bound to forgo,” grieved Isolde. “Our plans involve constructing the most wonderful fresh dwelling beside the stream; additionally, ball games will commence during the coming week, a sport you have yet to try, Nell. The thrill is immense. Furthermore, a fresh melody is on our schedule to master—Odette Pullen is currently refining her execution of it; moreover, Alice Pullen intends to transport a fresh Pansy volume in the upcoming week, which every one of us will recite in turn, taking a chapter each, beside the stream. Besides, your deep affection for reciting aloud is well known to you, Nell.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0076 }

Not a single thing altered Nell's decision. She had settled her thoughts. Going to school to Mr. Pidgeon again was something she would not do; upon returning home, she informed Thirza of this.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0077 }

“Nonsense,” Thirza said.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0078 }

“That is not nonsense whatsoever,” Nell stated, her serious, accusing gaze fixed upon Thirza. “Can you not comprehend, Thirza? A offense has been committed against me.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0079 }

“Fiddlesticks to being insulted! Tomorrow, you will attend school just like always.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0080 }

“Oh, no.” Nell gave a soft shake of her head. “I’m not returning, Thirza. I’ll study my lessons at home and I’ll be as well-behaved as I can manage and keep quiet continuously if it’s at all feasible. But I will not return to school, I promise you.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0081 }

Thirza observed what appeared to be resolute obstinacy staring from the diminutive face of Nell. It was clear to her that defeating this trait would prove difficult, yet she prudently decided to refrain from speaking any further at that moment.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0082 }

“This evening, I will go down to consult Agatha regarding the matter,” was her inner thought. “Attempting to reason with Nell at this moment is pointless. Given how overwrought she is, I suspect she possesses a dreadful streak of obstinacy when the mood strikes her. Based on what I can gather from her account, Mr. Pidgeon’s conduct has been somewhat overbearing. Expressing such a view to her directly, however, would be a mistake. I will simply discuss it with Agatha instead. Having put ten children through school, she should possess some insight into the situation. Moreover, she will undoubtedly have learned the entire tale by now.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0083 }

Mrs. Sowerby was discovered by Thirza knitting quilts with her customary industry and cheer.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0084 }

“I imagine you are aware of the reason for my visit,” she stated, looking somewhat embarrassed.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0085 }

Mrs. Agatha gave a nod.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0086 }

“Regarding Nell’s trouble at school, I suppose,” she remarked. “Tillie Gammon stopped by while coming home from school and mentioned it to me.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0087 }

“I am at a loss regarding her,” Thirza remarked. “She asserts that returning to school is out of the question. A child has never appeared so agitated to me. Ever since her schooling began, I have anticipated difficulties. The situation was progressing far too smoothly for it to endure, as I was well aware. Her nervous temperament is so pronounced. Agatha, what recommendation would you offer?”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0088 }

“Well, Thirza, because you’ve requested my counsel,” Mrs. Sowerby remarked pleasantly—she thoroughly enjoyed being consulted for guidance—“I would simply indulge her a bit to begin with, I really would. I reckon that Mr. Pidgeon made a mistake. Naturally, one shouldn't admit that to the youngsters, as you are aware. And naturally he was correct in chastising her yesterday when she lost her temper. However, today was another matter. Everyone else who arrived late ought to have faced chastisement alongside Nell, that is my opinion. Furthermore, I disapprove of forcing the girls to sit alongside the boys as a penalty. It lacks modesty. Tillie Gammon felt truly outraged. She supported Nell entirely and mentioned that every student did as well. Nell appears to be quite well-liked by them, for some reason. I failed to imagine she would fit in among them so successfully.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0089 }

“So you truly believe it would be best for me to allow her to remain at home,” Thirza remarked, thoroughly astonished.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0090 }

“Yes. That is I wouldn’t bring up school to her again until she brought it up herself. Rely on it, Thirza, she’ll calm down in about a week and be willing enough to return on her own, that’s what, whereas, if you forced her to return immediately, good Lord knows what whim or fit of temper she’d have next and cause more problems than ever. The smaller the scene created the better, as I see it. She won’t miss a great deal by staying away from school, for that matter. Mr. Pidgeon is not effective whatsoever as an instructor. The discipline he maintains is disgraceful, that’s what, and he ignores the little children while spending all his effort on those older pupils he’s preparing for Regent’s. He would not have secured the school for another year if his uncle was not a trustee—the real trustee, since he simply controls the other two completely, that’s what. I swear, I don’t know what education in this Island is turning into.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0091 }

Mrs. Agatha moved her head from side to side, as if to imply that matters would be handled far more effectively were she merely in charge of the Province's educational system.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0092 }

Following the counsel of Mrs. Agatha, Thirza ensured that returning to school was never again mentioned to Nell. Her studies took place at home, where she completed her tasks and engaged in play with Isolde during the crisp, purple dusk of autumn; however, whenever she came across Hugh Carrow along the pathway or saw him during Sunday-school, she walked past him with a freezing disdain that remained completely unthawed despite his clear wishes to make amends. Not even the attempts of Isolde to act as a mediator yielded any results. Nell had clearly resolved that she would despise Hugh Carrow for the rest of her days.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0093 }

Yet, to the same degree that she despised Hugh, she adored Isolde, devoting to her the full affection of her fervent small heart, which was just as strong in its affections as in its hatreds. During one dusk, as Thirza returned from the orchard carrying a basket filled with apples, she discovered Nell weeping inconsolably, seated by herself near the eastern window.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0094 }

“What on earth is wrong now, Nell?” she inquired.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0095 }

“Isolde is the reason,” wept Nell with abandon. “My love for Isolde is so immense, Thirza. Living without her will never be possible for me. Yet I am fully aware that upon reaching adulthood, Isolde is going to marry someone, depart, and abandon me. Oh, whatever will I do? That husband of hers is someone I despise—I simply despise him with a passion. My mind has been picturing the entire scenario—the ceremony and all the rest—with Isolde attired in pure white clothes, wearing a veil, and appearing every bit as gorgeous and majestic as a monarch; while I serve as her bridesmaid, also wearing a gorgeous gown featuring puffy sleeves, yet concealing a fracturing heart behind my grinning visage. And after that, saying farewell to Isolde—” At this point Nell completely lost control, weeping even more bitterly.
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0096 }

Thirza swung around rapidly so that her twitching face would not be seen; however, her efforts failed; she broke down into the closest chair, erupting into a laugh so genuine and unfamiliar that Obed, who was walking across the yard outdoors, stopped, utterly astonished. Before this moment, when had Thirza’s laughter ever sounded like that to him?
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0097 }

“Well, Nell Harcourt,” Thirza remarked the moment she regained her voice, “if it is necessary for you to borrow trouble, for pity’s sake choose a source closer to home. It certainly seems to me that you possess an imagination.”
{: #nw-v01-c15-p0098 }
